mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 3-month moving average compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.8% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending confidence and trigger negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE crosses above 4.8% in 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad-based consumer demand weakness that triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline in prior month, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO), manufacturing sector slowdown signals impending economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO declines > 0.5% in 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals accelerating inflation that triggers hawkish monetary policy expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in real GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates severe economic slowdown that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline in prior quarter, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.
